places.name: Henrietta's Table
places.description: Our signature Harvard Square restaurant celebrating fresh local farms, New England seafood, and hearty seasonal classics.

places.name: Noir Bar
places.description: Intimate cocktail lounge right inside The Charles featuring seasonal martinis, small plates, and an outdoor patio in warmer months.

places.name: Alden & Harlow
places.description: Beloved subterranean dining room on Brattle Street known for wood-fired plates, handmade pastas, and inventive cocktails.

places.name: Harvest
places.description: A Harvard Square institution tucked down a cobblestone walkway—modern New England tasting plates and an exceptional wine list.

places.name: Tatte Bakery & Café
places.description: Bright neighborhood bakery ideal for morning espresso, flaky pastries, tartines, and shakshuka steps from the hotel.

places.name: Grendel's Den
places.description: Cozy Harvard Square basement tavern since 1971 with comfort food, local drafts, and lively neighborhood atmosphere.

places.name: Pammy's
places.description: Critically acclaimed New American trattoria halfway between Harvard and Central Square—worth booking ahead for handmade pasta.

places.name: Harvard Yard
places.description: The iconic 17th-century grassy heart of Harvard University, framed by Widener Library, Johnston Gate, and brick Georgian halls.

places.name: Harvard Art Museums
places.description: World-class collections spanning Impressionism to modern art inside a stunning glass-roofed atrium. Free admission for all visitors.

places.name: Charles River Esplanade Path
places.description: Peaceful tree-lined riverfront path just 3 minutes south of the hotel—ideal for a morning jog or golden-hour stroll past the boathouses.

places.name: The Brattle Theatre
places.description: Beloved single-screen repertory movie house showcasing classic 35mm films, indie premieres, and late-night cult favorites.

places.name: Harvard Book Store
places.description: Locally owned Cambridge landmark since 1932 with a famous basement used-book room and frequent author readings.

places.name: Mount Auburn Cemetery
places.description: America's first landscaped garden cemetery—175 acres of hills, ponds, birdwatching trails, and panoramic Boston skyline views from Washington Tower.
